messages:
Maya: Quick thread — we need a tighter contract for traceability + stream termination at the API gateway. Current behavior attaches trace on connect but drops span on midstream aborts. Leads to orphaned traces and confusing SLO dashboards.
Oliver: +1. Can you outline concrete signals we want to preserve? trace-id, span-id, stream-id?
Maya: Ideally: persistent trace-id, per-stream span-id, and a final terminal event that indicates why the stream ended (client-cancel / upstream-fail / timeout / graceful-end).
Zack: How about propagation timing? Do we attach trace headers on the initial request only or re-emit on resume/hedge?
Maya: Re-emit on resume/hedge. We need the runtime to correlate fragments to the same logical call. Suggest headers: `x-rw-trace-id`, `x-rw-span-id`, `x-rw-stream-id`, and `x-rw-terminate-reason`.
Sophia: Thoughts on exposing `x-rw-terminate-reason` to customers? That leaks internal semantics. Maybe keep it internal to our telemetry and only expose a normalized status to clients.
Len: Agree — internal header for telemetry, and a documented `stream_status` field in trailers for public clients. Trailers would be HTTP/2/3 only though.
Oliver: Right — chunked transfer (HTTP/1.1) has no native trailers everywhere. We have to support both. For HTTP/1.1 we could send a final JSON chunk like `{"stream_status":"cancelled","code":"CLIENT_CANCEL"}`. Hacky but pragmatic.
Zack: That implies gateway must buffer enough to emit a trailer-chunk on graceful close. Memory pressure concerns for many concurrent short streams.
Maya: We can avoid buffering entire payloads — just allow a tiny trailer write without re-sending body. The runtime already supports streaming trailers in h2/h3; for HTTP/1.1 we add a small terminal chunk.
Sophia: How does this interact with retries and idempotency? If a midstream abort triggers a retry we must ensure the trace maps to the retry attempt and not double-count.
Len: Option A: new attempt gets new span-id but same trace-id and links to previous span via `x-rw-parent-span` header. Option B: reuse span-id if it's a resumeable continuation.
Oliver: My vote: new span-id per attempt, attach `x-rw-parent-span` linking. Easier for sampling and avoids confusing single-span-per-attempt semantics.
Maya: Agree with Oliver. Also need a metadata field `attempt_count` in telemetry.
Zack: Edge case: hedging where we fan out to two upstreams concurrently. We should mark which response won. Need a `winner` flag in the final event.
Sophia: Also, consider privacy: trace metadata may include prod tenant ids. Always strip PII before writing to logs, and ensure KMS for traces retention.
infra-bot: Note: new header names added to allowed list on WAF config in staging. Deploy scheduled 12:30 PST.
Maya: Implementation checklist: 1) trace header passthrough & re-emit on resume/hedge 2) span-per-attempt + parent link 3) terminal-event emission (trailers or final chunk) 4) telemetry fields: attempt_count, terminate_reason, winner_flag 5) update SLO dashboards to consume terminal events.
Len: Also add an ingress configuration to toggle final-chunk behavior per client (some legacy clients might break).
Oliver: API contract for customers: public `stream_status` in final event with values {"ok","client_cancel","upstream_error","timeout","fallback"}. Keep internal `x-rw-terminate-reason` richer.
Zack: Implementation note: add a thin in-memory table mapping `stream-id` -> current span metadata for 60s post-termination to correlate late telemetry. Cheap compared to full persistence.
Maya: SLO impact: should reduce orphaned-span noise. We can add a dashboard card showing terminal reasons distribution.
Sophia: Security: ensure these headers are not used for auth decisions. Treat them as metadata only.
Len: Backwards compatibility: if upstream doesn't support parent linking, still proceed — best-effort.
Oliver: TL;DR: we standardize headers, emit final-event for visibility, and link retries via parent spans. I'll draft an RFC PR with the header list + sample payloads for HTTP/1.1 chunk and h2 trailers.
Maya: Awesome — ping when draft is up. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
